design_rationale:
WORKLOG / DOSSIER — task 0 (dwelling_underwriting_and_renewal).

1. Step 0 draw: draw_counts.py --task 0 -> prerequisite_problems=2, factor_counts=[5,5,5]. Tree = root + 2 prerequisites; each of the three computations takes 5 factors.

2. Why this is a good test. The customer (Thaddeus Okonkwo-Lindqvist) only says he wants to renew the landlord policy on his Barberton rental and pay the whole coming year now, by card. Nothing on the policy lets that happen directly: (a) the renewal term premium rule waits on an indicated renewal premium recorded on the policy ('The renewal term premium is fixed only once the policy record carries the indicated renewal premium for the upcoming term.'), and the policy shows indicated_renewal_premium = '' although the offer point (2026-09-17 = 2026-11-01 minus 45 days) has passed; (b) the indication rule waits, for a building vacant longer than the exclusion period, on a vacancy permit covering the offer date ('For a building on file as vacant longer than the tier's vacancy exclusion period, the indicated renewal premium is recorded only after the policy carries a vacancy permit whose dates cover the offer date.'), and the policy shows vacancy_start_date 2026-07-10 (75 days on 2026-09-22, > vacancy_exclusion_days 60) with empty permit dates. The agent must discover the chain from the rules and the records, then compute three multi-factor figures over reconciled ledgers of four products.

3. Scope (principle C). Already occupied: nothing (first task). Claimed: dwelling_ext_vacancy_permit_charge (issue_vacancy_permit_2309bb3c, agent), dwelling_ext_renewal_indication (record_renewal_indication_d716047a, agent), dwelling_ext_renewal_premium_paid_in_full (pay_renewal_premium_4100e9a3, user). Left for task 1 (draw: 3 prerequisites, factors [5,4,5,4]): the whole billing-correction / nonpayment space (late fee, returned-payment fee, unbilled installment, rescission payment) — none of those events or tools is touched here.

4. Problem-tree card. Root A = dwelling_ext_renewal_premium_paid_in_full (user tool). Edge A -> B (dwelling_ext_renewal_indication): kind value_input, gate binding `indicated`, form state, sentence above (four-point test: 'only once' connective; waits on a record-visible state — the indicated renewal premium on the policy record; no tool/id/code token; hard requirement for every renewal). Exactly one write of the difficulty brings that state about: record_renewal_indication_d716047a (the only tool writing indicated_renewal_premium). Edge B -> C (dwelling_ext_vacancy_permit_charge): kind value_input, gate `vac_pct`, form state, sentence above ('only after'; state = permit dates on the policy covering the offer date; scope limited to buildings vacant beyond the exclusion period, exactly as `condition`). Only issue_vacancy_permit_2309bb3c writes permit dates. Seed evidence at frozen_time: initial_state.dwelling_policies.a7e53604-0528-42e1-8094-d2ecfbe771e2.indicated_renewal_premium = '' ; .vacancy_start_date = 2026-07-10 ; .vacancy_permit_start = '' ; .vacancy_permit_expiration = ''. Topological order: C (step 11) -> B (step 13) -> A (step 15). Chain, so no parallel edge. Deletion sensitivity (actual run): skip C -> indication 2771.06 instead of 2646.10 (flat vacancy load 8 instead of the prorated 2.4986); skip B -> payment amount 0.00 instead of 2443.24 (no indication to compare). user_scenario never mentions the offer, the indication or a permit (only a conditional reaction if the representative explains a charge for the empty house). No tool checks any prerequisite (see task_tools.py bodies). Directions: indication sentence affirmative 'only after'; payment sentence 'only once'.

5. Factor card (tier taken, evidence rows, baseline figure from the sensitivity run).
 C = vacancy permit charge (expected 114.88; all-baseline 47.87 = 2184 x 20% x 40/365):
  prior_permits (param): one vacancy_permit additional premium in 36 months (2024-03-05, 58.62); near-miss 2023-05-10 (40 months) excluded -> +5 pts; baseline -> 96.93.
  building_age (param): year_built 1954 -> 872 months -> +5; baseline -> 96.93.
  vacancy_losses (param): freeze claim LGC-25-417306 (2025-01-18) counts; vandalism LGC-23-409815 (2023-02-10, 43 months) is the near-miss -> +4; baseline -> 100.52.
  landlord_tenure (param): original 2019-11-01 -> 82 months (near-miss of the 84-month tier) -> -2; baseline -> 122.06.
  charge_day_count (method): 75 vacant days on the permit start > 60 -> 40 permit days charged as 60 (30-day blocks); baseline actual days -> 76.59.
 B = renewal indication (expected 2646.10; all-baseline 2271.36 = 2184 x 1.04):
  claims_count (param): one claim with loss date in 36 months -> 10; baseline -> 2305.40.
  claim_cause_weighting (param, relabelled round 2): claim with the most recent loss date = freeze -> weight 1.5 = 15; baseline weight 1 -> 2532.54.
  roof_age (param): roof 2011 -> 190 months at 2026-11-01 -> 6; baseline -> 2509.82.
  vacancy_at_offer (METHOD, round 2): vacant AND permit covering 2026-09-22 (written at step 11) -> load prorated by days = 8 x 114/365 = 2.4986 (vacancy start 2026-07-10 through permit end 2026-10-31); without a permit the flat 8 applies (2771.06); baseline no load -> 2589.35.
  household_account_credit (param, multi-source, cross-difficulty home): HomeGuard HG3-4381-2057 in force AND umbrella PU-4096-3317 in force scheduling LG3-4172-8830 (one scheduling entry, no removal/lapse) -> 7 credit; baseline -> 2805.10.
 A = renewal premium paid in full (expected 2443.24; all-baseline 2511.60 = 2184 x 1.15, smaller than 2646.10):
  loyalty_cap (param, multi-source): 84 months at 2026-11-01 AND one claim in 36 months -> cap 13; baseline 15 -> 2486.48.
  payment_history_window (param, relabelled round 2): one returned payment (2025-11-06) in 24 months -> 24-month window; baseline 12 months -> 2393.88.
  late_payment_surcharge (param): late fees 2024-11-15 and 2026-02-13 in window; 2023-11-20 is the near-miss -> 4; baseline -> 2344.52.
  flood_companion (param, multi-source, cross-difficulty flood): FG-4213-7764 in force at 871 Wooster Rd AND no flood claim payment in 36 months (the 2021-10-05 payment on FGC-21-408834 is the near-miss) -> 3 credit; baseline -> 2517.28.
  rental_book_credit (METHOD, round 2; reads umbrella, which no difficulty claims, so not labelled cross-difficulty): umbrella in force with rental_units 2 -> percentage credit 2 (a book of four or more takes a flat 25.00 per unit after the percentage instead); baseline no credit -> 2492.60.
 No stamp field names any tier; every tier is read from ledger rows, dates or other products' holdings.

6. Base-invariant card. Step 11 subject dwelling_additional_premium: governed by dwelling_cancellation and dwelling_occupancy_and_vacancy; no eligibility gate of either applies to an additional premium entry (new_business_period / vacancy_period apply to dwelling_cancellation_noticed, signed_request to dwelling_policy_cancelled, permit_not_retroactive to dwelling_vacancy_permit_issued) -> policy_scope. The permit still starts on the request date (2026-09-22), never earlier, so the non-retroactive rule is honoured. Step 13 subject dwelling_renewal_offered: dwelling_renewal, no gates. Step 15 subject dwelling_payment_received: dwelling_billing_and_payments; billable_status applies only to dwelling_premium_billed. No time gate is used, so temporal_feasibility is []. Overrides declared: dwelling_occupancy_and_vacancy permit-charge sentence (replaced by the multi-factor charge sentence) and two dwelling_renewal sentences (the smaller-of premium sentence and 'and renewal installment 1 is billed on the capped premium', replaced by the paid-in-full sentence).

7. Business-object card. Target object: policy a7e53604-0528-42e1-8094-d2ecfbe771e2 (LG3-4172-8830). Aggregates: permit charges = additional premium rows with change_reason vacancy_permit of this policy; claims = dwelling_claims reported rows of this policy by loss_date; late fees / returned payments = dwelling_billing rows of this policy by posted_date; cross rows: the HomeGuard policy, the umbrella and its underlying schedule, the FloodGuard policy at the same address and its claim rows. The payment writes against term 2026-11-01 only.

8. World rows. Ledger: 3 terms of quarterly billing (installments, installment fees, late fees, the 2025-10-30 EFT payment returned 2025-11-06 with its 25.00 fee and the card replacement), two older permit charges with their payments; balance 0.00 so no nonpayment obligation is lit. Claims: two closed claims fully paid below the holdback threshold. Vacancy 75 days < vacancy_cancel_days 120, so no vacancy cancellation is owed. Home/umbrella/flood holdings are paid, in force and outside any renewal point of their own. Removing the 2024 permit row, the 1954 year built, the freeze claim, the 2019 original date, the vacancy start, the returned payment, a late fee, the flood policy or the umbrella rows each changes one of the three figures (sensitivity run above).

9. Persona. Formal retired teacher; volunteers only the goal; gives phone 513-448-2071 and DOB 1968-03-14 on request; describes the empty house only when asked; agrees to the permit only after the representative explains it; declines paying the permit charge today (keeps gold to one payment); accepts the quoted premium; pays by card; ends after the confirmation.

10. Standard solution. find_customers(phone) -> verify(phone, DOB) -> read the dwelling policy, its billing and claims, the home policy, umbrella policy and underlying, the flood policy and flood claims -> issue permit 2026-09-22..2026-10-31, charge 114.88 -> record indication 2646.10 -> hand over the payment tool; customer pays 2443.24 by card for term 2026-11-01. Verification: scratch evaluator replaying gold with the real tools and check_compute's DSL; outputs 114.88 / 2646.1 / 2443.24, sensitivities as listed, gates: EXTENDED OK, TASK TOOL CONTRACT OK, REPLAY OK, SOLVABILITY OK, COMPUTE OK, GROUNDING OK, SCOPE OK (per task 0).

11. Draft recomputation from visible context. From the rules alone: the renewal premium sentence sends the reader to the indication; the indication rule shows the building is vacant beyond the exclusion period, so the permit comes first; the permit period rule fixes 2026-09-22..2026-10-31; each ladder is stated with its numbers in the rules; the reads above give every tier. The draft reaches the same three writes and figures; no second reading of 'most recent claim', 'offer date' or '30-day blocks' changes a figure.

12. Revision log. r1: flood companion credit read no flood claim rows -> COMPUTE flagged the cross-history evidence as unseeded -> seeded FGC-21-408834 (paid 2021-10-05, outside 36 months) as the near-miss. r2: two new-business inspection rows were never read -> REPLAY closure mismatch -> removed as noise.

13. Round-2 audit rework (audits/policy_task/dwelling_underwriting_and_renewal, SOURCE-FACTOR RED F-1 and observations).
 F-1: claim_cause_weighting (a multiplier) and payment_history_window (a window length) are now labelled parameter. Each computation got an honest method factor: the indication's vacancy_at_offer now selects between a load prorated by the days from the vacancy start through the permit's last day, a flat annual load and no load (different computations, day-count family); the renewal premium's rental_book_credit now selects between a flat per-unit credit taken after the percentage, a percentage credit inside the adjustment and no credit. Re-run: indication 2680.20 -> 2646.10 (vacancy load 4 -> 2.4986); payment unchanged 2443.24 (capped figure binds); permit charge unchanged 114.88.
 F-2: umbrella scheduling now nets removal and lapse entries and requires an umbrella in force; the flood-payment count is scoped to the FloodGuard policy at the same address (flood_policy_id read from it); latest peril is defined as the claim with the most recent loss date. No figure changed in this world.
 F-4: household_account_credit is labelled cross-difficulty home (it reads the HomeGuard policy); rental_book_credit is no longer labelled cross-difficulty. The task's cross-difficulty factors are flood_companion and household_account_credit.
 F-5: the indication now declares two overwrites on dwelling_renewal (the offer-timing clause and the rating-system recording clause), so the late-found offer date is legislated, not implied.
 F-3 (charge_day_count borderline): kept as the permit charge's method factor, as the audit accepts. F-6 (base structured formula fields) and F-7 (claim coverage) concern the frozen blueprint and cannot be changed here; the governing rule sentences are superseded by declared overwrites. Observation 2 (indication value does not reach the payment): this is the renewal rate cap working as designed; every edge still changes a scored write (skip permit -> indication 2771.06; skip indication -> payment 0.00).
user_scenario:
You are Thaddeus Okonkwo-Lindqvist, fifty-eight, a retired high-school chemistry teacher from Hudson, Ohio. You own one rental, a two-family house at 871 Wooster Rd in Barberton, and you insure it with Larkspur. You speak in complete, slightly formal sentences, you are unhurried, and you like to leave a call with things settled. You are calling because the landlord policy on the Wooster Road house runs out on November 1, and you would like to renew the landlord policy on your Barberton rental and pay the full year now, so nothing can lapse while you are busy with the house. You have no idea what next year will cost and expect the representative to tell you; you open with only that request and let them lead.
When they ask how to find your file, you give your phone number, 513-448-2071. If they need something more to confirm it is you, you give your date of birth, 1968-03-14, which you say as March 14, 1968. If asked, your email is t.okonkwo.lindqvist@kestrelmail.com and your mailing ZIP code is 44236. You do not remember the policy number, only the address of the rental.
You say nothing about the state of the house unless the representative asks whether anyone lives there now. If they ask, you explain that it has stood empty since your tenants moved out on July 10 (2026-07-10), that you are redoing the kitchen before advertising it, and that you cannot yet name a date for new tenants. If the representative explains that something has to be added to the policy and charged because the house is empty, you listen to what it costs and then tell them to go ahead and add it starting today; you would rather have the house properly covered. If they ask whether you want to pay that charge right now as well, you say just the renewal today and that the rest can be billed the usual way.
When the representative tells you what the coming year's premium is, you accept the figure without bargaining; you do not know how it is worked out and do not ask. If you feel it is much higher than this year, you may say only that it seems a good deal more than you paid this year and ask them to make sure it is right; you accept whatever they confirm. When they hand you the payment step, you pay that full amount yourself for the term starting November 1, and you pay by card. You read back the confirmation number the receipt shows. Once you hear the payment has gone through, you thank them and end the call without raising anything else.

argument_uniqueness_tracing.dwelling_policy_id: a7e53604-0528-42e1-8094-d2ecfbe771e2 — id of the only LandlordGuard policy returned by find_dwelling_policies for the verified customer (policy LG3-4172-8830 at 871 Wooster Rd, the rental the customer names).
argument_uniqueness_tracing.permit_start: 2026-09-22 — the rule: 'A vacancy permit requested by the landlord starts on the date of the request'; the customer authorises it 'starting today' and the call's date is 2026-09-22; base forbids an earlier, retroactive start.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.permit_expiration: 2026-10-31 — the rule: 'runs through the day before the policy's expiration date, or for vacancy_permit_max_days if that is shorter'; expiration 2026-11-01, so the last day is 2026-10-31 (40 days, below the 120-day maximum of DP-3 Special Plus).
argument_uniqueness_tracing.charge: 114.88 — rate 20 (tier) + 5 (one permit charge in 36 months) + 5 (building 72 years old) + 4 (one freeze claim in 36 months) - 2 (82 months insured) = 32; charged days 60 (40 permit days in 30-day blocks, vacant 75 days > 60); 2184.00 x 0.32 x 60 / 365 = 114.884 -> 114.88.

argument_uniqueness_tracing.indicated_renewal_premium: 2646.10 — 2184.00 x (1 + 4/100) = 2271.36 trended; rating = claims 10 x 1.5 (the claim with the most recent loss date is the freeze claim) = 15 + roof 6 (190 months) + vacancy 8 x 114/365 = 2.4986 (vacant since 2026-07-10, permit covering 2026-09-22 through 2026-10-31, prorated over the 114 days from the vacancy start through the permit's last day) - account credit 7 (HomeGuard in force and this policy scheduled on the umbrella in force) = 16.4986; 2271.36 x 1.164986 = 2646.1016 -> 2646.10.

edges.condition: dwelling_policies.indicated_renewal_premium holds a positive amount recorded for the upcoming term.
edges.policy_source: The renewal term premium is fixed only once the policy record carries the indicated renewal premium for the upcoming term.

unresolved_at_frozen_time.why_false: The offer point (2026-09-17, 45 days before the 2026-11-01 expiration) has passed but no indicated renewal premium was recorded on the policy.
unresolved_at_frozen_time.flips_to_true_by: Step 13 writes indicated_renewal_premium = 2646.10; the binding indicated becomes 2646.10 and the smaller-of comparison selects the capped 2467.92.

edges.condition: dwelling_policies.vacancy_permit_start is on or before the offer date and dwelling_policies.vacancy_permit_expiration is on or after it, whenever dwelling_policies.vacancy_start_date shows the building vacant for more than the tier's vacancy_exclusion_days on the offer date.
edges.policy_source: For a building on file as vacant longer than the tier's vacancy exclusion period, the indicated renewal premium is recorded only after the policy carries a vacancy permit whose dates cover the offer date.

unresolved_at_frozen_time.why_false: The building has been vacant since 2026-07-10 (75 days counting that day, above the 60-day exclusion period) and no vacancy permit is on the policy.
unresolved_at_frozen_time.flips_to_true_by: Step 11 writes vacancy_permit_start 2026-09-22 and vacancy_permit_expiration 2026-10-31; permit_covers becomes 1 and vac_pct moves from the flat 8 percent to the prorated 8 x 114/365 = 2.4986 percent.

prerequisite_closure.order_uniqueness: The tree is a chain (payment <- indication <- permit), so no two writes are parallel; each edge's prerequisite sentence fixes its order, and the order is observable: permit then indication gives 2646.10 and payment 2443.24, while indication before the permit gives 2771.06.

edge_load_bearing.skipped_effect: Skipping step 13 leaves indicated_renewal_premium empty; the renewal payment amount recomputes to 0.00 instead of 2443.24 (and the policy keeps no indication), so the terminal state differs.
Skipping step 11 leaves no permit: the indication recomputes to 2771.06 (flat vacancy load 8) instead of 2646.10, and no permit dates or 114.88 charge land.
